The game has next to no content compared to Euro Truck Simulator 2 (ETS2). I purchased it after reading raving reviews about how it was just like ETS2, but it had a different atmosphere and better graphics. Yet there are only two truck manufacturers, and the amount of road you can explore is a joke. There is the same amount of road in France and Germany alone for ETS2. For the price of this game, definitely not worth buying such a limited experience. Especially not since the two expansions, New Mexico and Oregon, are 12 dollars each. Please do not waste your money if you're not a really die hard fan and wouldn't mind the comparatively small amount of content.

A flawed but enjoyable semi-sequel to Euro Truck Simulator 2.

Do not buy this if you have not played Euro Truck Simulator 2. ETS2 is a superior game in nearly every way and you should play that first.

If you are like me though, and you greatly enjoyed ETS2 and are looking for something similar but new, this is it.

Pros:
Handful of new trucks
Totally different landscape
Cities look very nice
Game feels so close to ETS2 you can jump right in

Cons:
Map takes less time to traverse
Time acceleration means more stops than ETS2
Cops are more obnoxious than speed cameras

Really needs a bit more refinement and more area to be a great game. As is, still good.

Edit: Distance scaling change has been a big improvement. Need more trucks now.

I've already written a review for this game back in 2017, but since it became so outdated and not worth updating anymore, I just took it down. Today, I have passed the 1000-hour mark. I'm sure the map will be complete one day. I'll be buying all of the DLCs to show my support, but mostly because the vast majority of them is actually worth it. Game is lacking a few features, but it's so mod-friendly that all of them can be manually fixed. Even I, despite not being a modder, can easily create my own truck skins, even if I'm doing it in a weird way (by replacing the in-game textures with mine). But hey, it works and the game allows for these mods to be made and imported! I'm so glad I've been there from the start. Best decision I've made. I've bought all of the DLCs when new, so even if the combined value is huge now, it's usually less than 20€ a year. It has to be just a few cents per hour played. I do not regret a single cent that I invested into this game and I will invest many more. Long live the American Truck Simulator!

When I'm driving the Kenworth W900 i can almost smell papaws aftershave and hear nanny telling him to switch lanes or he will miss his turn. I never thought I'd like this game and I certainly never expected a video game to make me pause and reevaluate my life, but here I am. This is more than just a game to me. It's like coming home.

For many years this was my go-to for a relaxing game to enjoy after a long day at work. With introduction of Driving Academy this changed. Sure, these challenges can be fun and enrich the game for some. It may even be helpful for new players to get going. Even I took some notes after more than 1000 hours on virtual roads. Making those scenarios mandatory for 100% achievements however completely destroyed ATS's position as a hallmark for a game to play to relax and enjoy scenery. 

Prior to addition of Driving academy, "completing" the game consisted of exploring new states and enjoy new landscapes. With its addition, Driving Academy takes away enjoyment and replaces it with tediousness to get ATS's full experience. I wasn't a fan of Truck Driving Basics being "mandatory" back when they were released, but played along, becoming startled the first time after many years. With recently added Truck Driving Proficiency scenarios, I became actually annoyed with ATS. So much that after more than 1500 hours I decided to put it on hold for an indefinite period.

I am extremely disappointed by SCS's decision to make such a frustrating experience part of the "completion" process of the game and I sincerely hope they remove all achievements connected to Driving Academy to return ATS to its great state.
